recognize_zh: 中央大細胞約為旁邊小淋巴球的三到四倍大，核圓略偏心、染色質細緻，細胞質豐富、淡灰藍色帶細小空泡且邊緣不規則起伏，符合血中反應性組織球（reactive histiocyte）。
features: Large cell, about 3-4 times the diameter of adjacent small lymphocytes
Low N:C ratio with an oval, slightly eccentric nucleus
Finely reticular chromatin without prominent nucleoli
Abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm with fine vacuoles and a darker blue peripheral rim
Irregular cytoplasmic border with small blebs; no phagocytosed organisms or cells
Background crenated red cell aggregates and small lymphocytes
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a large mononuclear cell, three to four times the size of neighboring small lymphocytes, with a low N:C ratio, an oval slightly eccentric nucleus with fine chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli. The abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm is finely vacuolated with an irregular, blebbed border. No ingested organisms or hematopoietic cells are identified. Findings are consistent with a circulating reactive histiocyte (macrophage); a search for intracellular organisms and phagocytosed cells is recommended in the clinical context.

ddx.vs: Monocytes are smaller with folded, indented nuclei, lacy chromatin and gray cytoplasm containing fine azurophilic granules.
Hairy cells are smaller (about twice a lymphocyte) with circumferential fine hair-like projections and are CD103/CD11c/CD25-positive.
Plasma cells have coarse clock-face chromatin, deep basophilic cytoplasm and a distinct perinuclear hof.
Hemophagocytic macrophages contain ingested red cells, platelets or nucleated cells, which are absent here.
